note: review article; two-column PDF layout interleaved and symbols garbled in the conversion (a hazard in itself); keys follow the original content

qs.q: Where are the first sharp diffraction peak (FSDP) and the principal peak (PP) of silica glass located, and in which kind of data do they appear?
qs.a: FSDP at Q of about 1.5 per angstrom in both X-ray and neutron data (periodicity of about 4 angstrom, coherence length about 10 angstrom); PP at about 3 per angstrom appears in the neutron data but is not observed in the X-ray data

qs.q: Why is the principal peak positive in the neutron structure factor but negative in the X-ray one?
qs.a: The partial structure factors S_O-O and S_Si-Si have positive peaks near 3 per angstrom while S_Si-O has a negative one; neutrons weight O-O heavily (0.543) so the peak is positive, while for X-rays the Si-O weight (0.498) dominates, giving a negative peak

qs.q: Which of the two glasses densified to the same density is the more ordered by the FSDP, and what does the ring entropy say?
qs.a: Both have density 2.7 g/cm3 (hot-densified 1200 C at 7.7 GPa, HDG; cold-densified room temperature at 20 GPa, CDG). By FSDP height HDG is the most ordered and CDG the most disordered. Yet HDG has the highest ring entropy of the glasses made at 7.7 GPa, i.e. strong topological disorder; the authors stress this conceptual difference between FSDP order and ring-entropy order

qs.q: Is the cold-densified glass permanently densified?
qs.a: No. Its density decreases to 2.21 g/cm3 after heat treatment at 900 C

qs.q: How is ring entropy defined and what values do the crystals and glasses take?
qs.a: H = minus the sum of F_n ln F_n over ring sizes n (F_n the fraction of n-fold rings); zero when all rings have the same size. Both cristobalites have only sixfold rings so H=0; alpha-quartz (six- and eightfold rings) has H=0.45; the silica glasses have larger H; coesite's H is similar to the glasses'

qs.q: Do the ring persistence A and ring entropy H distinguish crystalline from non-crystalline silica?
qs.a: No. Both are insensitive to the crystal/glass distinction: crystals and glasses can show similar values (coesite and the silica glasses cluster together), which is why the authors call them a unified framework for crystalline and non-crystalline materials

qs.q: Can the FSDP and principal peak be reproduced by a single tetrahedron model?
qs.a: No for glassy silica (neither FSDP nor PP is reproduced by a tetrahedron). For liquid CCl4 only the third peak Q3 is reproduced by a CCl4 tetrahedron; the model gives a single PP whereas experiment shows two because of orientational correlations

qs.q: What type of article is this: new experimental results or something else?
qs.a: A review of the authors' group's recent results (the journal labels it REVIEW) on combined quantum beam diffraction and topological analysis of silica polymorphs, not a new single experiment

qs.q: What is the thermal conductivity of the densified silica glasses?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Thermal conductivity is not discussed

qs.q: What photon energy was used at the SPring-8 beamline for the X-ray measurement?
qs.a: NOT STATED. The facilities (SPring-8, J-PARC) are named but no beam energy is given in the text
